title: GitHub Actions pull_request triggers (.github/policy.rego): omit 'types' when it lists only GitHub's default opened, synchronize, reopened
answers: Why did Conftest fail saying the pull_request trigger lists GitHub's default activity types?
How do I add a pull_request or pull_request_target trigger to a workflow with a paths filter without listing types?
Can I still restrict pull_request_target to labeled or closed events, or add extra types on top of the defaults?
Where is the check that flags redundant default activity types on pull request triggers?
body:
Path: .github/policy.rego:deny_redundant_default_pull_request_types checks the `on:` trigger block of every workflow file for `pull_request` and `pull_request_target`, reading `input["true"]` (YAML's `on:` key parses as boolean true), and is where trigger-level type lists are validated by Conftest.
Rule: When a trigger's `types` set is exactly {opened, synchronize, reopened} (order and duplicates ignored), the policy denies it and the fix is to delete the `types:` key so GitHub applies the same defaults. Subsets, supersets such as adding `labeled`, and an omitted `types` key are not flagged by this rule; keep them as written.
Constraints: Applies to the `on.pull_request` and `on.pull_request_target` triggers only; push, schedule and workflow_dispatch are not checked. Deleting `types` must leave the rest of the trigger (paths, paths-ignore, branches) untouched, as the 16 workflow edits in this change did. The default set is a constant (`default_pull_request_types`) in the same policy file, so any change in GitHub's defaults means editing that constant.
applies: Workflow YAML under .github/workflows that declares pull_request or pull_request_target triggers, checked by Conftest with .github/policy.rego; not the job-level or step-level rules.
says: Conftest says my pull_request trigger lists GitHub's default activity types and should drop them
Can I add a pull_request trigger with a paths filter without listing the activity types?
Can pull_request_target still be limited to labeled or closed events, or extra types added to the defaults?
Which policy check flags redundant default activity types on pull request workflow triggers?
search: GitHub Actions pull_request and pull_request_target trigger policy: a types list exactly equal to opened, synchronize and reopened is denied as redundant and should be deleted. Supersets, subsets and omitted types are not flagged; push, schedule and workflow_dispatch are not checked.
